Example: If value = 0, we may show a static image of the video. If value = -1, you allow any preview length.

bing-ai-performance.text: AI Performance in Bing Webmaster Tools The AI Performance Report in Bing Webmaster Tools shows how your site’s content is used in AI‑generated answers across Microsoft Copilot and partner experiences by highlighting which pages are cited, how visibility trends change over time, and the grounding queries associated with your content. Which AI Experiences Are Included? AI Performance reflects grounding and citation activity across the following supported AI surfaces: Microsoft Copilot AI-generated summaries in Bing Select partner AI integrations What Does AI Performance Measure? AI Performance shows how your content is cited in AI‑generated answers across supported AI experiences by summarizing and aggregating citation activity across three core areas of visibility. Pages Cited in AI Answers Shows how often a specific URL from your site is visibly cited in an AI‑generated answer. Average Cited Pages The average number of unique pages from your site that were cited per day in AI‑generated answers across supported AI experiences during the selected date range. Grounding Queries Your Content Appears In Shows the key phrases the AI used when retrieving content that was cited in its answer. Page-Level Citation Activity Citation counts by specific URL that show which pages from your site are cited most frequently across AI-generated answers during the selected date range. This view reflects how often pages are cited, not their importance, ranking, or role within a response. How Does AI Visibility Change Over Time? The timeline view shows how your site’s citation volume changes over time across supported AI experiences. This view helps you observe overall trends in how often your content is cited in AI‑generated answers during the selected date range. Changes in citation volume may reflect shifts such as: Changes in the volume or type of user questions Updates to your content System or model updates across AI experiences NOTE These trends reflect aggregated citation activity only and cannot be attributed to a specific cause or event. Changes in citation trends are observational and do not indicate the impact of any single update, model change, or content modification. Available time ranges : 7 days 30 days 3 months Custom range (within available historical data) How are AI Performance Metrics Calculated? AI Performance measures visible citation activity to show how often your content is referenced in AI-generated answers across supported AI experiences. Total Citations The total number of times your content was visibly referenced or shown as a source in AI‑generated answers during the selected date range. Cited pages The number of unique pages from your site that were cited on a given day. Average cited pages The average number of unique pages that were cited per day over the selected time range. NOTE AI Performance does not measure rankings, authority, performance, or importance. It simply shows which content was cited. What Are Grounding Queries in the AI Performance Dashboard? The grounding queries tab shows the key phrases the AI used when retrieving content that was referenced in AI-generated answers. How to read the Grounding Queries tab Each row in the grounding queries tab in Bing Webmaster Tools displays a short phrase. These phrases are grouped representations from your site that were retrieved and cited in AI-generated answers. They are not full user questions or prompts. What the data shows : The number shown for each grounding query reflects how often content from your site was referenced in AI answers for that phrase during the selected time range. Higher numbers mean your content was referenced more frequently in AI answers associated with that grounding query. A single grounding query can be associated with multiple pages from your site. A single page can appear under multiple grounding queries if it was referenced in different AI answers. How to use Grounding Query data In AI Performance, grounding queries are shown as grouped phrases with associated citation activity across AI-generated answers. Use grounding queries to: Understand which phrases are most often associated with your site being cited in AI answers. See patterns in how your content is referenced across AI experiences. Identify areas where your site already has strong AI visibility, and where it may be limited. Example: How a Grounding Query is shown in AI Performance If content from your site is referenced in AI answers related to solar energy, that activity may appear under grounding queries such as “solar energy” or “solar panels.” These grouped phrases summarize related activity across multiple AI answers rather than showing individual questions. Important Notes: A single grounding query may be associated with multiple pages from your site, and a single page may appear under multiple grounding queries. Grounding queries group citation activity under common phrases to surface recurring themes and areas of visibility across AI‑generated answers. Grounding queries reflect aggregated activity across AI‑generated answers, not individual user questions or specific answers. Grounding queries may be determined differently across supported AI experiences and partners, and the phrasing shown may vary. Data is provided at a summary level and does not show individual AI answers, exact prompts, or why a specific page was referenced. Page–Level Citation Activity The Pages view (list by pages) in AI Performance shows which pages from your site are most cited in AI‑generated answers during the selected date range. This view helps you : See which pages are cited most often across AI‑generated answers. Compare citation activity across pages on your site. Understand how citation activity is distributed at the page level. Grounding Query - Page Mapping connects the Grounding Queries and Pages views within the AI Performance report so users can quickly see which pages are being cited for a specific grounding query, and which grounding queries are driving citations to a specific page. Select a grounding query to view its cited pages, or select a page to view its associated grounding queries. NOTE One grounding query may be mapped to multiple pages and vice-versa. NOTE The Pages view reflects aggregated citation counts only. It does not indicate ranking, authority, importance, or a page’s role within an individual AI answer. Data Availability and Refresh Cadence AI Performance shows citation activity across supported AI experiences for the selected date range. Data is refreshed daily, with a short processing delay, and reflects aggregated citation activity over time. Historical data is available only for the time ranges shown in the dashboard. About the Data in AI Performance AI Performance data is aggregated and summarized to provide a representative view of citation activity across supported AI experiences. The data shown is not a complete log of every instance where content may have been referenced. As a result: Not all citation activity may appear in the dashboard. Very low or infrequent citation activity may not surface. Totals may differ across views (for example, between pages, grounding queries, and time‑series charts). The data shown represents a sample of overall citation activity. Results may be refined as additional data is processed. AI Performance is designed to support trend analysis and comparative insights over time, rather than precise accounting of individual AI answers or prompts. As with Bing search, AI Performance reflects only content that is eligible for indexing. Bing respects all content owner preferences expressed through robots.txt and other supported control mechanisms. Downloading AI Performance Data You can export AI Performance data for deeper analysis, including: Grounding query data with citation counts Page‑level citation data Time‑series metrics across custom date ranges Exports are available in CSV and Excel formats. Using AI Performance to Improve Your Visibility AI Performance can help highlight potential areas to review when thinking about how your content appears in AI‑generated answers. The following are general content best practices you may consider when using this data: Align content with user intent Review the grounding queries and pages associated with your site to understand the types of information your content supports in AI answers. Strengthen depth and expertise Pages cited across related grounding queries often reflect clear subject focus. Expanding coverage in related areas can reinforce clarity and usefulness. Improve clarity and structure Use descriptive headings, concise sections, tables, and FAQ-style content to make information easier to understand and reference in AI answers. Support claims with evidence Including examples, data, and cited sources can improve clarity and trust when content is reused in AI‑generated answers. Keep content fresh and accurate Regular updates help ensure AI systems reference current, relevant information. Maintain consistency across formats Ensure text, images, and other media describe the same products, entities, and concepts. For deeper guidance on structuring content to improve inclusion in AI‑generated answers, see Optimizing your content for inclusion in AI search answers . FAQs Why do my citation counts change over time? Citation volume changes based on user demand, content freshness, model updates, partner refresh cycles, and shifts in the topics users ask about. Do citations represent clicks or traffic? No. A citation indicates that your content was visibly referenced or shown in an AI-generated answer. It does not represent traffic, clicks, or user engagement. Why are some of my pages never cited in AI Answers? There are multiple reasons why content may not surface in AI‑generated answers. A page may not appear if it is less relevant to common user questions, lacks clarity or depth, is outdated, or is outperformed by other sources. Why do grounding queries look short or vague? AI Performance shows grouped, generalized phrases used to summarize citation activity across AI‑generated answers. It does not display individual user questions or highly specific long‑tail queries. This helps provide a clearer, higher‑level view of how your content appears across common subject areas in AI answers. Do AI Performance metrics match traditional search metrics? No. Grounding and citations show how AI systems use your content to generate answers. This differs from traditional search metrics, which measure rankings, clicks, and traffic. Why do I not see any grounding queries for my site? Grounding queries may not appear if there is limited aggregated citation activity for your site during the selected date range. Because grounding queries summarize citation activity across AI‑generated answers, very sparse or infrequent citations may not surface in the dashboard. This is expected and does not indicate a penalty or exclusion. In Grounding Query – Pages Mapping, can I filter by a grounding query and a page at the same time? No. You can filter only by one at a time. Export the filtered data for further cross-referencing. In Grounding Query – Pages Mapping, does filtering affect exports? Yes. Exports reflect the currently applied filter. Can I see which pages are cited for a specific grounding query? Yes. Select a grounding query to filter the report. The view updates to show pages cited for that query with their citation counts. Can I see which grounding queries lead to a specific page being cited? Yes. Select a page to filter the report. The view updates to show grounding queries associated with that page. Why might citation counts for the same grounding query and page differ depending on how I filter? AI Performance data is sampled, and grounding queries and pages may each be sampled over slightly different time windows within your selected date range. This means filtering by a grounding query and then viewing a page may show a different citation count than filtering by that page and viewing the same grounding query. This is expected and does not indicate missing or incorrect data. Does filtering affect exports? Yes. Exports reflect the currently applied filter. AI Performance - Intents, Topics and Citation Share FAQ Bing Webmaster Tools is expanding the AI Performance Report with four preview capabilities – Intents, Topics, Citation Share, and Compare – that help publishers move beyond citation counts to better understand query context, thematic visibility, and relative citation presence. These preview capabilities add new ways to analyze AI visibility in the AI Performance Report: Intents classify grounding queries by query intent, Topics group related queries into broader themes, and Citation Share shows your site’s relative presence within the citation space for a specific grounding query Intents What are Intents? Intents classify grounding queries in the AI Performance Report by query intent–for example, Informational, Commercial, Navigational, Learn and Solve, Research, Creation, Local, and more. This helps publishers better understand the broader search context associated with their citation appearances, not just the individual query text. What intent categories are used? We use a modern intent taxonomy that goes beyond the traditional informational, navigational, and transactional categories. Examples include: INTENT Informational Media Navigational Commercial Learn and Solve Research Live Event Local Comparison Planning Utility Creation Conversational Other How are Intents assigned? Intent labels are assigned by AI/ML classifiers that analyze the grounding query and its context. How accurate are the intent labels? The classifiers are continuously improving. In some cases, a grounding query may be assigned an intent label that does not perfectly match how you would characterize it, particularly for ambiguous or multi-intent queries. How should I use Intents? Identify where your site is appearing. If your site is monetized through e-commerce, strong citation activity for Commercial or Comparison intents can help you understand whether your content is appearing in commercially oriented AI experiences. Spot intent gaps. If you expect to see citation activity for Research queries but mostly see Informational ones, that may indicate an opportunity to add more depth, supporting evidence, or clearer coverage for research-oriented topics. Align content structure to query intent. Different intents may benefit from different content formats, such as comparison tables for Comparison, step-by-step guidance for Planning, or concise explanations for Informational queries. These insights can help inform content planning, but they do not guarantee citation outcomes. Topics What are Topics? Topics group related grounding queries into broader thematic clusters, such as Solar Energy, Home Renovation, or Cloud Security. This helps publishers understand which larger subject areas are driving citation activity for their site in AI-generated answers. How are Topics different from grounding queries? Grounding queries are the individual phrases shown in the AI Performance Report. Topics sit one level above them by grouping related grounding queries under a common theme. Example: Topic : Solar Energy Grounding queries under this topic : "solar panels," "solar energy efficiency," "residential solar installation" Can I filter by a topic and see which pages are cited? This is possible by exporting the data and then applying filters. How are Topics assigned? Topics are assigned by AI/ML classifiers that analyze related grounding queries and group them into thematic clusters. How accurate are Topics? The classifiers are continuously improving. In some cases, a grounding query may be grouped into a topic that feels like an imperfect fit, especially for niche or highly specialized domains. We expect the quality and precision of Topics to improve as the classifiers mature. How should I use Topics? Identify strong subject areas. Topics can help you see which themes are associated with the most citation activity for your site. Discover content gaps. If a topic is generating citation activity but your coverage is limited, that may indicate an opportunity to add more depth, supporting evidence, or related content. Guide content planning. Topics turn query-level AI Performance data into a more thematic view, which can be especially useful for teams that plan around audiences, themes, or editorial areas rather than individual keywords. Citation Share What is Citation Share? Citation Share shows the percentage of citations attributed to your site out of all citations shown for a specific grounding query. It helps publishers understand not just whether their content was cited, but how much visibility it received within the full set of cited sources for that query. How is Citation Share different from total citations? Total citations tell you how often your content is cited. Citation Share tells you what percentage of the citation space your site receives for a specific grounding query. A site may have a high total citation count but a lower Citation Share when citation activity for the same query is distributed across many sources. METRIC WHAT IT TELLS YOU Total Citations Volume - how often your content is referenced overall Citation Share Relative citation presence - your share of citations for a specific grounding query Does Citation Share show me who my competitors are? No. Citation Share does not expose competitor domain names or identify which other sites hold the remaining share. It is designed to show your site’s relative citation presence for a grounding query without revealing other sites’ data. How should I interpret my Citation Share number? High and stable share → Your site is receiving a consistent share of citations for that grounding query. High but declining share → Citation activity may be becoming more distributed across sources. Review whether your content could benefit from updates, deeper coverage, or clearer structure. Low share on a core query → Your site is receiving a smaller portion of the citation space for a query that matters to you. Consider whether the content could be made more complete, current, or easier to understand. Growing share → Your site is receiving a larger share of citations over time. This may reflect changes in content, user demand, the broader web ecosystem, or AI system behavior. Important: Citation Share reflects citation activity. It does not represent rankings, traffic, or a quality score. Changes in share can be driven by many factors, including shifts in user demand, content changes across the web, model updates, freshness signals, and partner refresh cycles. Can Citation Share tell me if my content changes are working? Citation Share can help you observe whether your share changes over time after content updates, but it does not establish a causal link. Citation patterns can be influenced by many factors, including user demand, freshness, model behavior, partner refresh cycles, and changes across the broader web. Improving content quality, structure, and freshness can help strengthen your content, but it does not guarantee a specific citation outcome. Compare What is Compare? Compare is an analytics feature in the AI Performance Report that lets you overlay a previous time period on the same chart as your current view. It helps you visually observe how citation metrics have changed over time. Your current period displays as a solid line and the comparison period as a dashed line, both day-aligned on the same axis. What comparison options are available? You can compare against the previous period (e.g., last 30 days vs. the prior 30 days) at various durations. A custom option lets you pick any two date ranges manually. How should I use Compare? Before and after content updates. Observe whether citation activity changed after you updated, expanded, or refreshed content. Compare date ranges. Compare citation activity across standard or custom date ranges to understand whether visibility patterns are increasing, decreasing, or remaining stable. Does Compare tell me why metrics changed? No. Compare shows what changed between two periods, but it does not explain why the change happened. Citation activity can be influenced by many factors, including user demand, freshness, model updates, partner refresh cycles, and changes across the broader web. Compare helps you observe patterns, not establish causation. I have feedback or questions about these features. How do I reach the team? You can use the feedback option using an easy to use UI within the AI Performance Report or reach out through standard Bing Webmaster Tools support channels. Your feedback helps us improve the quality, coverage, and usefulness of these preview capabilities and reporting tools over time.

anthropic-crawlers.text: All Collections Privacy and legal Does Anthropic crawl data from the web, and how can site owners block the crawler? Does Anthropic crawl data from the web, and how can site owners block the crawler? April 7, 2026 Copy for LLM As per industry standard, Anthropic uses a variety of robots to gather data from the public web for model development, to search the web, and to retrieve web content at users’ direction. Anthropic uses different robots to enable website owner transparency and choice. Below is information on the three robots that Anthropic uses and how to set your site preferences to enable those you want to access your content and limit those you don’t. Bot Use What happens when you disable it ClaudeBot ClaudeBot helps enhance the utility and safety of our generative AI models by collecting web content that could potentially contribute to their training. When a site restricts ClaudeBot access, it signals that the site's future materials should be excluded from our AI model training datasets. Claude-User Claude-User supports Claude AI users. When individuals ask questions to Claude, it may access websites using a Claude-User agent. Claude-User allows site owners to control which sites can be accessed through these user-initiated requests. Disabling Claude-User on your site prevents our system from retrieving your content in response to a user query, which may reduce your site's visibility for user-directed web search. Claude-SearchBot Claude-SearchBot navigates the web to improve search result quality for users. It analyzes online content specifically to enhance the relevance and accuracy of search responses. Disabling Claude-SearchBot on your site prevents our system from indexing your content for search optimization, which may reduce your site's visibility and accuracy in user search results. As part of our mission to build safe and reliable frontier systems and advance the field of responsible AI development, we’re sharing the principles by which we collect data as well as instructions on how to opt out of our crawling going forward: Our collection of data should be transparent . Anthropic uses the Bots described above to access web content. Our crawling should not be intrusive or disruptive . We aim for minimal disruption by being thoughtful about how quickly we crawl the same domains and respecting Crawl-delay where appropriate. Anthropic’s Bots respect “do not crawl” signals by honoring industry standard directives in robots.txt. Anthropic’s Bots respect anti-circumvention technologies (e.g., we will not attempt to bypass CAPTCHAs for the sites we crawl.) To limit crawling activity, we support the non-standard Crawl-delay extension to robots.txt. An example of this might be: User-agent: ClaudeBot Crawl-delay: 1 To block a Bot from your entire website, add this to the robots.txt file in your top-level directory. Please do this for every subdomain that you wish to opt out from. An example of this is: User-agent: ClaudeBot Disallow: / Opting out of being crawled by Anthropic Bots requires modifying the robots.txt file in the manner above. Alternate methods like blocking IP address(es) from which Anthropic Bots operates may not work correctly or persistently guarantee an opt-out, as doing so impedes our ability to read your robots.txt file. If a crawler has a source IP address on this list , it indicates that the crawler is coming from Anthropic. You can learn more about our data handling practices and commitments at our Help Center . If you have further questions, or believe that our Bots may be malfunctioning, please reach out to [email protected] . Please reach out from an email that includes the domain you are contacting us about, as it is otherwise difficult to verify reports. openai-web-search.text: Responses *+*]:mt-3"> Copy Page Web search Allow models to search the web for the latest information before generating a response. Responses Copy Page Web search allows models to access up-to-date information from the internet and provide answers with sourced citations. To enable this, use the web search tool in the Responses API or, in some cases, Chat Completions. There are three main types of web search available with OpenAI models: Non‑reasoning web search: The non-reasoning model sends the user’s query to the web search tool, which returns the response based on top results. There’s no internal planning and the model simply passes along the search tool’s responses. This method is fast and ideal for quick lookups. Agentic search with reasoning models is an approach where the model actively manages the search process. It can perform web searches as part of its chain of thought, analyze results, and decide whether to keep searching. This flexibility makes agentic search well suited to complex workflows, but it also means searches take longer than quick lookups. For example, you can adjust reasoning levels on models like gpt-5.5 to change both the depth and latency of the search. Deep research is a specialized, agent-driven method for in-depth, extended investigations by reasoning models. The model conducts web searches as part of its chain of thought, often tapping into hundreds of sources. Deep research can run for several minutes and is best used with background mode. Use gpt-5.5 with reasoning set to high or xhigh . Choose an integration Use case Recommended path Notes New web search integration Responses API with web_search and gpt-5.5 Supports hosted web search controls such as filters, sources, live-access control, and longer research runs Existing Chat Completions search integration Chat Completions with gpt-5-search-api Use this only when you need to preserve a Chat Completions integration Multi-step research or long-running reporting gpt-5.5 with high or xhigh reasoning Use background mode for reports that can take several minutes Using the Responses API , you can enable web search by configuring it in the tools array in an API request to generate content. Like any other tool, the model can choose to search the web or not based on the content of the input prompt. For new Responses API integrations, use { "type": "web_search" } . The earlier web_search_preview tool remains available for legacy integrations, but it does not support newer controls such as filters , external_web_access , and return_token_budget . The action is one of: search , which represents a web search. It will usually (but not always) includes the search queries which were searched. Search actions incur a tool call cost (see pricing ). open_page , which represents a page being opened. Supported in reasoning models. find_in_page , which represents searching within a page. Supported in reasoning models. Keep the default for most requests. Set it to unlimited only for high-effort research or evaluation runs that need to inspect many pages and might otherwise stop at the standard returned-token cap.
